maria_g: kicking off a concurrency sweep on eval-runner-v2 (model: opt-1.3b-quant) — seeing throughput drop after 48->64 concurrent streams. p95 still okay but qps tanks.
kevin_l: hmm. dropped requests or queueing? any logs showing errors?
maria_g: logs show a bunch of 'evicting kv-cache entry' and a new metric 'runner.dropped_by_backpressure' increments. no explicit errors, just ops counters.
zhou: can you paste the sweep config? might be the batch-window tuning or max inflight tokens.
maria_g: config pasted:```yaml
runner: eval-runner-v2
model: opt-1.3b-quant
concurrency_sweep: [8,16,32,48,64,96]
per_stream_seq: 1024
batch_window_ms: 12
max_inflight_requests: 256
warmup_iters: 100
metrics: [qps,latency_p50,latency_p95,dropped_by_backpressure]
```
ash: batch_window_ms 12 seems aggressive for long seqs. at higher concurrency batcher might close windows early and cause inefficient packing -> items spilled to fallback fastpath?
sam_t: also check KV cache eviction policy. If streams exceed KV capacity, we start thrashing and latency P95 stays but throughput collapses.
kevin_l: good points. maria, can you run a quick probe with batch_window_ms=40 and max_inflight_requests=512? compare token/s and dropped counters.
maria_g: doing that now. triggering job in CI: <https://ci.internal/runs/4182> (PR: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/4123>)
ci-bot: Job #4182 queued for branch maria/eval-sweep-tune — runner-tests (linux, gpu)
maria_g: preliminary: with batch_window_ms=40 and max_inflight_requests=512 we still see some drops at 96 concurrency but throughput improved ~18% at 64. dropped_by_backpressure still exists but lower. attaching short sample of metrics: qps: [8->96] = [120,230,400,620,740,810] ; dropped:[0,0,1,4,18,60]
zhou: interesting shape. suggests transient backpressure that scales nonlinearly. do we see any networking queue saturations on the host? i/o util?
ash: also check the runner's batching code for early-exit when batch size below min_pack. there was a recent change to prefer latency that might force smaller batches under contention.
kevin_l: @ash can you grep commit history for 'min_pack' or 'prefer_latency' in last 2 weeks?
ash: will do. quick grep shows commit 6f9a2c modified batcher windowing to short-circuit under low fill. link: <https://git/repo/commit/6f9a2c>
sam_t: can we add a transient counter 'batcher.short_circuit_count' to correlate? would help separate algorithmic short-circuits vs backpressure drops.
maria_g: good idea. I can add a lightweight counter in the harness and re-run one sweep locally.
kevin_l: also we should reconcile metrics between local harness and CI. I noticed CI's job aggregates qps differently (sum of per-worker qps) while local uses a global token counter, so dropped counters look inconsistent. this is causing flaky regressions in perf tests.
zhou: yes — redefine canonical "qps" for eval CI: must be total served tokens / effective runtime (excluding warmup) and expose both per-worker and global counters. file a tiny RFC?
kevin_l: I'll open an RFC and a follow-up PR to change CI dashboards. ACTIONS: 1) maria add batcher.short_circuit_count + KV eviction counter to harness (ETA today). 2) maria run sweep with batch_window_ms=40,80 and max_inflight 256/512 and post metrics. 3) ash audit batcher commits and flag risky changes. 4) kevin open RFC for canonical qps definition + ci wiring fix.
maria_g: starting on (1) now. posting logs to slack thread when done.
ci-bot: Job #4182 started on runner-gpu-12
maria_g: quick update: added batcher.short_circuit_count, re-ran 64/96 points locally. short_circuit_count spikes at 64->96 correlating with dropped_by_backpressure. full raw metrics: <https://dash/reports/metrics/1790043210>
kevin_l: perfect. this points to the short-circuit heuristic being too eager under high multiplexing. let's revert that heuristic in a patch and test again.
ash: I'll prototype a softened heuristic: require short-circuit only if avg_batch_fill < 0.2 AND inflight_tokens < threshold.
sam_t: if we revert heur, add a guard in CI that flags regressions only if global qps drop >5% and dropped_by_backpressure >10 events in steady window. reduces noise.
zhou: can we also produce a small dashboard panel for 'cost_per_token' overlayed with qps so product teams can see unit economics impact of these tuning decisions?
kevin_l: agreed, add cost_per_token (cpu+gpu time estimate / tokens) to the eval dashboard. I'll take that.
maria_g: thanks all — will push a PR for short-circuit tweak + add counters, link here when green.
kevin_l: wrap-up: prioritize fixing batcher heuristic -> re-run sweep in CI with canonical qps. if still flaky, escalate to infra for host-level diagnostics. :thumbsup:
_meta: generated for dataset: slack eng-ml thread about eval harness concurrency sweep and metric mismatches
